cards.text: This psalm is "For the choirmaster. Of David." David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), opens with someone he calls the fool, and the fool is saying something not out loud, just in his heart. You know, like that reply you write to your boss in your head and NEVER send.

cards.question: Deep down in his heart, the fool has settled something about God. What is it?

answers.text: That God is on his side
That God owes him a favor

cards.text: Then David zooms out from one fool to a whole crowd: "They are corrupt; their acts are vile." Friend, I've had burnt batches get better reviews than that.

cards.question: Even in that corrupt crowd, David says a few people are still out there doing good.

cards.text: Now look up. The LORD looks down from heaven upon the sons of men, scanning everybody, like me going through a whole tray hunting for ONE cookie that came out right.

cards.question: When the LORD looks down from heaven upon the sons of men, what is He looking for?

answers.text: Anyone who understands and seeks God
Anyone strong enough to fight for Him
Anyone who brings Him the best gifts

cards.text: So the LORD looks over the sons of men, every single one. Now David tells us what He finds.

cards.question: When the LORD's search is done, David says only the fools have turned away, and everyone else is doing fine.

cards.text: Verse 4 asks, "Will the workers of iniquity never learn?" They devour "my people" like bread, and I bet that question comes out through gritted teeth.

cards.question: Those workers of iniquity devour the people like bread. What else do they refuse to do?

cards.text: But then the whole thing flips, and the ones doing all the devouring are overwhelmed with dread. Not so tough now, are they?

cards.question: Why are the workers of iniquity overwhelmed with dread?

answers.text: God is in the company of the righteous
A great army is marching toward them
Their own king has turned against them

cards.text: Then the psalm turns and talks right to the sinners, the ones who frustrate the plans of the oppressed. Messing with people who are already being pushed down? That's LOW, friend.

cards.question: The sinners frustrate the plans of the oppressed, and that leaves the oppressed with nowhere safe to turn.

cards.text: The last verse turns into a longing, a big "Oh, that" moment, as David looks ahead to what he wants to see come for Israel.

cards.question: In that last verse, what is David longing to see come for Israel?

answers.text: A new king rising in Israel

cards.question: When the LORD restores His captive people, David calls for ___ in Jacob and Israel.

findings.problem: Card 7 repeats card 5. Card 5 already told that the LORD looks down from heaven upon the sons of men and scans everybody. Card 7 says it again ("So the LORD looks over the sons of men, every single one") and adds no new moment from the passage. It is a recap card.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Rest from every war" is close in meaning to the right answer "Salvation coming from Zion". The salvation of Israel can be read as deliverance from enemies, so a baker could argue that rest from war is part of it.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
